    How the ranking works

    The user-rating blend gives Steam 75% of the weight and Metacritic PC users 25%. Both scores are required for the default blend. The optional Available ratings mode uses the remaining source at 100% weight, skips thresholds only for missing review values, excludes games without either usable pair, and labels reduced coverage. A usable pair needs a score and a positive count. Recorded scores and counts still obey their active thresholds even when the other value is missing. Other thresholds and setup preferences still apply. Missing default blends sort last. The recommended view starts at Steam >=90% with >=1,000 reviews, and Metacritic users >=8/10 with >=100 votes.

    Suggested ranges are app presets: Steam 80-90%, 100-1,000 reviews; Metacritic 7-8/10, 25-100 votes. Defaults use the upper endpoints. Critics and Ally guide ratings are separate filters. High ratings cannot establish setup suitability. Setup checks independently cover gameplay, art style, Steam purchase availability, Windows, play mode, offline use, couch controls and original Z1 Extreme viability. The current matches disclose any unknown or failed check. This is a review shortlist, not a hardware/offline certification.

    Green badges mean Steam lists shared/split-screen play. Online co-op alone does not qualify. Known turn-based and known pixel/voxel games are hidden initially. Exclusion badges identify Turn-based, Pixel art and Voxel style using the same evidence as the filters; inferred classifications say "inferred". Choose "Browse all", then the Exclusion tag filter to inspect these games. Search and comma-separated exclusions also accept these tag names. An absent badge does not establish suitability. Other gameplay and art styles can remain unknown; use the supported-only filters when this matters. Solo/co-op/versus choices preserve your other filters. "Browse all" explicitly clears filters and setup preferences while retaining manually hidden games.

    Data completeness

    This is a saved catalog, not all games on Steam or all guide pages. The source archive contains 849 candidates and 701 guide references. Only matched Steam and Metacritic products belong in this catalog; a guide is optional. Current coverage is computed above. Research and edition review remain incomplete; missing captured pages do not prove that pages do not exist. Imported catalogs may use a different candidate pool.

    Sources and snapshot dates

    Legacy catalog records may contain U+ character-level transcriptions from an earlier ASCII profile; their original source bytes are not available in this candidate. Refresh those records from verified sources before relying on exact names. New imports preserve valid UTF-8 text.

    Every game has Steam and Metacritic links. ROG Ally Life coverage is optional. Scores, prices and availability can change. Prices use US dollars. Generic Ally guides do not establish original Z1 Extreme performance. The filters cover recorded facts, not every source-site option. Multiplayer details use explicit PC publisher statements: capacity in a described mode, split-screen, co-op campaign and drop-in support. Unknowns do not pass positive filters. Co-Optimus helped identify useful feature groups; individual Co-Optimus game records were unavailable during this collection. LAN capacity requires an explicit source and refers to separate connected PCs, not couch play. ESRB labels, cross-play and other unsupported facets are not fabricated. Steam required age is a distinct store field, not an ESRB rating. Guide power/resolution/VRAM filters use recorded profiles only; estimates never qualify as source evidence.

    SteamMetacriticROG Ally LifeCo-Optimus PC directory
    How estimated settings work

    Every game has an estimated trial profile for the original Z1 Extreme. Similar guide-backed games are chosen by shared genres/developer, nearby release year, explicit publisher engine declarations and similar minimum RAM when available. Each contributes one resolution and VRAM vote. Published minimum RAM of 16 GB or more triggers a conservative texture/preset starting point and shared-memory advice; it is not an Ally compatibility test. Missing comparisons use a conservative generic baseline. Power, preset and FPS goal follow explicit tuning rules.

    All estimates are low confidence. They are not optimal settings, benchmark results, exact-device verification or proof that an option exists. They never fill review scores, review counts, prices, offline status or controller capabilities. Missing facts have explicit next steps instead of invented values. Guide filters remain source-only.

    Start at 25 W on AC, using a 30 W Turbo option only when supported by the dock/charger. Test a demanding scene and adjust one setting at a time. An FPS target is a goal to test, not a performance prediction. Analogy sources and ASUS hardware guidance are linked in each estimate.

    Your file, updates & recovery

    This HTML contains the app, current data, a previous data snapshot and your saved choices. It uses no account, server, browser storage or automatic updates. Use Save this HTML after changing your shortlist or filters, then keep the downloaded copy. Browser "Save page" is not the app's save workflow.

    Keep a dependable copy

    A compatibility copy is larger and keeps the games as plain text, so it opens even in a browser that cannot unpack compressed (gzip) data. Reset clears filters, saved games and hidden games in this tab; Undo is available.

    Update the catalogue

    1. Press Export data JSON, then edit the downloaded copy in a text editor (a worked example is in Help, under How to update this).
    2. Select the edited file below and read the preview before you apply it.
    3. Press Save this HTML to keep the update.

    Review affected games

      Files are limited to 12 MB. Validation checks structure and links, not whether supplied facts are true. The preview names affected games and fields, replaced settings, changed evidence and filters that would reset. Expand Review affected games to inspect the full list. If you change your choices after previewing, Apply refreshes the preview for another review first. A failed update restores the prior data, choices, page and Undo history. The previous snapshot remains available after you save.

      Maintenance notes

      The readable code inside this HTML is grouped into Domain, Decision, Estimates, Provenance, Technical, Multiplayer, Archive review, Portable and Interface modules. Decision keeps evidence and setup eligibility separate from review ranking. Estimates recomputes a low-confidence trial profile from the current catalog; estimates never replace facts or count as test passes. Filters share one registry. The exported JSON uses format rog-game-catalog, schema 1, and a data object with ordered fields, rows, ratingsObserved and metadataObserved. A row follows the field order exactly; unknown metrics use null. The guide field may be null; guide profiles, rating and date require a guide link. Keep each game's Steam ID stable so saved choices survive an update. An optional evidence map adds dated, scoped records by Steam ID; older schema 1 files without it remain supported and their missing checks stay unknown. Evidence notes explain inference explicitly. Failed pacing or visual records may carry exclusionTags with turn-based, pixel-art or voxel identifiers; the identifier must match the evidence kind. This drives badges, search and tag filtering without duplicating classification data. Profiles may include optional details (label, device, tdp, resolution, vram, settings) containing captured source text or explicitly labeled narrative summaries. Use v16.5 or later to preserve these details through updates and saves; older schema 1 profiles without details remain accepted. An optional provenance map groups source context by Steam ID and field names: provider, source, observed, outcome, confidence, platform, edition and note. Each field can occur only once per game. Missing provenance stays unknown; update previews warn before dropping field source context. An optional technical map retains dated publisher requirement excerpts, parsed minimum/recommended RAM and explicitly declared engines by Steam ID. Technical evidence also survives saves, imports and recovery; previews warn if it would be lost. An optional multiplayer map retains per-field PC source claims by Steam ID: localPlayers, onlinePlayers, lanPlayers, comboPlayers, splitScreen, dropIn and campaign. Each record has value, source, observed, platform, edition and note. Missing records mean unknown; numeric zero or boolean false require an explicit unsupported statement. Player counts describe a reported mode, not necessarily every mode. These facts survive saving and recovery; update previews disclose lost records. An optional archiveReview stores a dated historical candidate/guide inventory and omission explanations with source outcomes. It does not certify live availability or admit games. The Missing a game section shares the title search above. Older imports may omit this context; the preview warns before dropping explanations. Completeness is recomputed from the installed data.

      Catalog, choices, exports and saved HTML preserve valid Unicode source strings. Legacy U+... labels are interpreted only in display and search, and interpreted displays carry the ⟦U+⟧ marker; stored labels remain unchanged. Imports reject malformed UTF-8 and unpaired UTF-16 surrogates. Search recognizes exact text and its accent-insensitive folded form, including the interpreted view of legacy U+ notation. An incomplete numeric/date entry or overlong search blocks matches and saving until corrected. Invalid saved choices reset to safe defaults. Damaged current data can recover from the embedded previous snapshot. Neither mechanism invents missing facts, repairs damaged application code, nor guarantees recovery from corruption of both copies. Keep an untouched HTML backup before editing code.

      Help
      

      How to update this
      

      A. Change the games (the catalogue). The games are stored inside this file as compressed (gzip) data. Do not edit that block by hand: in a text editor it is unreadable letters. Edit an exported copy instead.
      

        

      1. Scroll to the bottom of the page and open Your file, updates and recovery. Under Update the catalogue, press Export data JSON. A file called HandheldHunter PC Games-Catalog-schema1.json downloads.
        2. 

      2. Open that file in any text editor (Notepad works). It is one very long line, so use Find (Ctrl+F) to reach a game.
        3. 

      3. Worked example. Search for "Portal","400". A little further along you will see ,null,98.5,199707,8.8,6178,. The 98.5 is the Steam score. Change it to 97.5. Change only the number: keep every comma, quote and bracket. Save the file. (The number straight after the game's web link and null is always the Steam score.)
        4. 

      4. Back in the page, press Select updated data JSON and pick the edited file. Read the preview: it lists each game that would change and says what. Press Apply this update (or Cancel). Undo is available.
        5. 

      5. Press Save this HTML in the top bar and keep the downloaded copy. That copy now holds your update.
        6. 

      

      Check it worked: search for Portal and look at its card. Do not touch anything else in the file. Files over 12 MiB are refused. The line "Catalogue content" in the footer comes from a small readable block named content-meta (version, date, source); you may edit those words by hand in a text editor, but never the compressed directory-data or directory-backup blocks.
      

      B. Change the colours. Open the file in a text editor and search for --accent-light. Two values set the accent colour in every look: --accent-light for Paper and --accent-dark for Charcoal and True Black. Text on accent buttons uses --on-accent-light and --on-accent-dark. Example: change #8A3C53 to another dark colour. Keep light text readable on it, and leave the games alone.
      

      C. Update the app itself. Replace the file with the new version and open it. Your saved games, saved views and Look stay, because the browser keeps them. Your filters and hidden games live inside the HTML copy you saved, so they do not move to a new file by themselves: save a copy first, and keep it.
      

      What lives where
      

      The compare list and your shortlist (saved games) live in the open page. Compare is never saved. Your shortlist, saved views and Look choice are also remembered by this browser, so a reload keeps them. Hidden games and filters are kept only if you press Save this HTML and keep that copy. Nothing is sent anywhere and there is no account.
      

      Keep it
      Press Save this HTML (one button, in the bar at the top) after you change filters or saved games, then keep the downloaded copy. Your original file stays unchanged. Export data JSON saves the catalogue alone.
      

      Delete it
      Reset my choices (in the same footer section) clears filters, saved games and hidden games in this tab, and Undo brings them back. To remove everything, delete the files you downloaded. Delete a saved view with its Delete button. To forget your saved games, your Look choice and every saved view at once, clear this site's data in the browser.
      

      Compare
      Press Compare on two to four games. When the second game is added, the comparison opens over the page with a button "Close and go back to the game". When it is closed, a bar at the bottom of the screen shows "Compare (2): open" so you can look again. It shows the user rating blend (Steam 75%, Metacritic users 25%), tags, source links and retrieval dates. A value that is not recorded says so.
      

      Saved views and links
      Save current filters stores a named set of filters in this browser (up to 20). Export views writes them to a file and Import views reads such a file back. The address of this page also carries the current filters after the # sign, so you can bookmark or share them; it never carries saved games, hidden games or your compare list.
      

      Search and counts
      Search checks titles, genres and tags, and also accepts close spellings when nothing matches exactly. The number in brackets beside a filter option shows how many games it would list, given your other filters. A game with several genres or tags counts once under each, so those counts can add up to more than the total.
      

      Printing
      Print prints the page of results that is open (up to 24 games). Closed details are opened and the address of every source link is written out after the link. Your choices are not printed.
      

      Catalogue version and date
      

      Sources
      Every game shows where its figures came from and when they were retrieved. Ratings and prices change, so check the linked pages before you buy.
      

      Glossary: words used in this app
      

      Z1 Extreme
      The processor chip in the original ROG Ally handheld. Settings advice here is for that chip.
      

      D10 and XInput
      XInput is the standard Xbox-style controller mode that most PC games expect. D10 is the label this app's setup checks use for the controller setup it assumes (Xbox-style controls on the TV); no source in this file defines it further.
      

      VRAM
      Memory set aside for graphics. The Ally shares its main memory, so a bigger VRAM setting leaves less for the game.
      

      W (watts)
      The power limit for the chip. Higher can mean more speed and more heat and fan noise.
      

      Metacritic users
      Scores from ordinary players on the Metacritic site, out of 10. Not the critics.
      

      Evidence
      A dated, sourced note that a game passes or fails a check, for example that it supports split-screen. "Unknown" means nobody recorded it.
      

      Profile
      One set of recorded graphics settings (power, resolution, VRAM) from a guide page for a game.
      

      Snapshot
      The catalogue as it was on a date. This file also keeps the previous snapshot so a bad update can be undone.
      

      Compatibility HTML
      A larger saved copy that stores the games as plain text, so it opens even where compressed data cannot be unpacked.
      

      gzip, JSON
      gzip is a way of compressing data. JSON is a plain-text format for data that a text editor can open.
      

      Hash sign (#)
      The part of the web address after the # sign. Here it carries your current filters.
      

      

      Technical notes
      

      Import size
      Import accepts a JSON file up to 12 MiB. An export of the catalogue is about 5 MB, so it imports with room to spare.
      

      File size
      This file is about 1.1 MB. The embedded catalogue of 739 games with their sources, its backup copy and the embedded fonts account for most of it, which is above the 1 MB tier for a single page. That is a recorded exception: the catalogue is the product and cannot be split into a lighter page without a server. It opens slowly on a slow connection.
      

      How close spellings work
      When nothing matches exactly, each word may differ from the start of a word in the game by one edit when it has 5 to 8 letters, or two edits when it has 9 or more. An edit is an insertion, a deletion, a substitution or swapping two neighbouring letters (the optimal string alignment distance). Short words must match exactly. This is original code in this file, not a library.
      

      Counts for power, resolution and VRAM
      These three are counted together: because all three must match one recorded guide profile, each option shows how many games would be listed if you chose it while keeping your other two choices. Single-choice lists such as release status add up to the total.
